oewn-06526084-n.learner: a record of things that happened in the past, or a story that tells about them
examples: Mr. Wickham should invent such a history of himself as he gave me last night

oewn-15146348-n.learner: all the things that have happened in the past, taken together
examples: It was the worst storm in the town's history.

oewn-06165265-n.learner: the subject that records past events involving people and explains what they mean
examples: She is studying history at university.

oewn-15148913-n.learner: the whole line of events, one after another, running from the past to now and even on into the future
examples: think rather of Memling at one end of the history of painting and Meissonier at the other

oewn-06166450-n.learner: everything that is remembered of the past because it was written down; the knowledge this makes up
examples: The first cities were built near the dawn of recorded history.

oewn-00772482-v.learner: to make someone do something, or make them act in a certain way
examples: what can have induced him to behave so cruelly?
nor will such behaviour as this ever induce me to be explicit.

oewn-01647592-v.learner: to cause something to start or come about
examples: The news induced a crisis in the government.
The doctor decided to induce labour.

oewn-00638103-v.learner: to reason from single cases to a general rule, or to show that a rule is true in this way
examples: From these cases, the scientist induced a general law.

oewn-01741298-v.learner: to make an electric current by using electric charges or magnets
examples: Moving a magnet through a coil of wire induces a current.

oewn-01796596-v.learner: to cause someone deep sorrow, or to make them unhappy
examples: The supposition did not pain her.

oewn-00070587-v.learner: to hurt someone's body and make them feel sick or unwell
examples: His old wound still pains him in cold weather.
he voluntarily acknowledged that the necessity of his absence had been self-imposed.
she then told him what Mr. Darcy had voluntarily done for Lydia.

oewn-00815640-v.learner: to talk with other people about something, or talk it over in detail
examples: They met several times, for there was much to be discussed.
The looks and behaviour of everybody they had seen were discussed

oewn-01036184-v.learner: to look closely at a subject in what you say or write
examples: The second chapter discusses the causes of the war.

oewn-06790941-n.learner: a funny story or remark meant to make people laugh
examples: He told a joke and everyone laughed.

oewn-00428583-n.learner: a silly or strange act that someone does for fun
examples: For a joke, they hid his shoes in the garden.

oewn-05180970-n.learner: something so small or silly that it should not be taken seriously
examples: Everyone thought his plan to run for mayor was a joke.

connotation.why: dismisses its target as not worth taking seriously

oewn-00431990-n.learner: playful activity that is full of good humour
examples: She said it half in joke, half in earnest.

oewn-00721817-n.learner: the work that a person or group is given, must do, or is expected to do
examples: there I readily engaged in the office of pointing out to my friend the certain evils of such a choice.
if you decline the office, I will take it on myself.

oewn-03847186-n.learner: a room or building where people do professional work or paperwork
examples: She works in an office near the station.

oewn-00587299-n.learner: a job or position in an organization
examples: He held the office of treasurer for ten years.

oewn-13968154-n.learner: being in power, said of a government or a government official
examples: During his first year in office, he cut taxes.

oewn-08369230-n.learner: the people who do professional work or paperwork in an office

oewn-08354251-n.learner: a department of a government that manages some of its business
examples: The Foreign Office issued a statement about the crisis.

oewn-01035490-n.learner: a religious ceremony or service set down by church leaders
examples: The priest read the office for the dead.

oewn-00864347-v.learner: to speak or write against someone or something very strongly

oewn-01121587-v.learner: to start an attack on someone, or to start fighting or a war with them
examples: The army attacked the town at dawn.

oewn-01122487-v.learner: to set on someone to hurt them, in their body or in their feelings
examples: A man attacked him in the street and took his wallet.

oewn-01120867-v.learner: to act first and go forward against the other side
examples: The visiting team started to attack in the second half.

oewn-00348264-v.learner: to start work on a task and put a lot of energy into it
examples: She attacked the pile of letters as soon as she got home.

oewn-00019785-v.learner: to begin to harm or damage something
examples: This disease attacks the lungs.

oewn-00579031-a.learner: in agreement with something, or steady and reliable
examples: "This fine account of him," whispered her aunt as they walked, "is not quite consistent with his behaviour to our poor friend."

oewn-01203638-s.learner: the same all the way through in how it is made up
examples: Stir the paint until its colour is consistent, with no streaks.

oewn-00466504-a.learner: having parts that fit together in an orderly, logical, and pleasing way
examples: The novel builds a consistent world in which every detail fits.

oewn-01873946-a.learner: able to be made or done again in the same way
examples: The results were consistent: other labs got the same numbers when they repeated the test.

oewn-02548492-v.learner: to do what a person, rule, or order tells you to do
examples: Elizabeth obeyed; and, running into her own room for her parasol, attended her noble guest downstairs.
